recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-31838 unless BR&R later reopens broader SubstanceDefinition.relationship cardinality decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-31838 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request asking that the relationship.type element be mandatory because a relationship is not meaningful without its type. The accepted resolution was "Will make type mandatory" for R5, with a 9-0-0 vote.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied before this reconciliation. The Jira snapshot records that the change was applied in the R4B branch and main build, and current-ancestry git commit 930304138e847067f6d142e431ddbed359e6baa6 changed SubstanceDefinition.relationship.type from min=0 to min=1 while citing FHIR#31838. R4B-ancestry commit 720a623d27bb5c37693fe620d8d2904802d6bce0 carries the same issue-tagged change.
additional_context: The current build uses SubstanceDefinition rather than an active SubstanceSpecification source entry. source/fhir.ini actively registers substancedefinition=SubstanceDefinition and assigns it to BR&R, while the current source tree has no active substancespecification entry. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-31838 and the relevant SubstanceDefinition relationship terms found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The authoritative current source, source/substancedefinition/structuredefinition-SubstanceDefinition.xml, already defines SubstanceDefinition.relationship.type with min=1 and max=1.
